laws.title: Hands-Free Driving Law
laws.subtitle: ID Code §49-1401A — No handheld devices while driving
laws.fullDescription: Idaho does not have a statewide ban on holding or using handheld electronic devices while driving. Idaho bans texting while driving but does not have a full hands-free law. Handheld calls are legal for adult drivers.
laws.penalty: $75 fine (texting only banned).
laws.exceptions: Emergency 911 calls are exempt from hands-free requirements.

quiz.q: Is handheld phone use banned while driving in Idaho?
quiz.explanation: Idaho: only texting while driving is banned in Idaho; handheld calls are legal.

laws.title: Non-Resident Hunting & Fishing License
laws.subtitle: Idaho Code §36-405 — Non-residents must purchase licenses
laws.fullDescription: Non-residents must obtain a valid Idaho hunting or fishing license before taking game or fish. Annual non-resident fishing licenses cost approximately $13.75; hunting licenses cost approximately $185.50. Some species require additional tags.
laws.penalty: Class B misdemeanor or felony; fines up to $1000 plus equipment forfeiture.
laws.exceptions: Residents are exempt from non-resident fees.

quiz.q: What is the penalty for hunting without a license in Idaho?
quiz.explanation: Hunting without a license in Idaho is a Class B misdemeanor with fines up to $1000.

laws.title: Impaired Driving (DUI/DWI)
laws.subtitle: Idaho Code §18-8004 — 0.08% BAC limit
laws.fullDescription: Idaho prohibits operating a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. Commercial drivers: 0.04%. Drivers under 21: 0.02 BAC. Implied consent laws apply.
laws.penalty: First offense: $1,000 minimum fine, 90–180 day license suspension, up to 6 months jail. Subsequent offenses carry mandatory minimums and longer suspensions.
laws.exceptions: None — even prescription medication impairment can result in DUI charges.

quiz.q: What BAC triggers a DUI in Idaho for regular drivers?
quiz.explanation: The legal BAC limit in Idaho is 0.08% for regular drivers, consistent with all US states.

laws.title: Open Container Law
laws.subtitle: Idaho Code §23-505 — No open alcohol in vehicles
laws.fullDescription: Idaho prohibits open alcoholic beverage containers in the passenger area of motor vehicles on public roads. Open container law applies to driver and passengers.
laws.penalty: $250 fine; applies to driver and passengers.
laws.exceptions: Passengers in for-hire vehicles (taxis, limos) may be exempt.

quiz.q: Can passengers drink alcohol in a private car in Idaho?
quiz.explanation: Idaho's open container law applies to all vehicle occupants.

laws.title: Recreational Cannabis — Not Legal
laws.subtitle: Idaho Code §37-2732 — Cannabis fully illegal — no medical program
laws.fullDescription: Idaho: Idaho is one of few remaining states with no medical or recreational cannabis program. All cannabis possession is illegal. CBD with less than 0.3% THC is permitted.
laws.penalty: Possession under 3 oz: misdemeanor, up to 1 year. Over 3 oz: felony.
laws.exceptions: Medical patients exempt.

quiz.q: Is recreational cannabis legal in Idaho?
quiz.explanation: Idaho has no cannabis program — all possession is illegal.

laws.title: Medical Cannabis — Not Legal
laws.subtitle: Idaho Code §37-2732 — Medical cannabis program
laws.fullDescription: Idaho has no medical cannabis program — Idaho is one of the few states without any form of legal cannabis.
laws.penalty: Any cannabis possession: criminal charge.
laws.exceptions: Registered patients are exempt from possession penalties.

quiz.q: Does Idaho have a medical cannabis program?
quiz.explanation: Idaho does not have a medical cannabis program.

laws.title: Firearm Carry Law — Constitutional
laws.subtitle: Idaho Code §18-3302 — Constitutional state
laws.fullDescription: Idaho is a constitutional state. Idaho passed constitutional carry for residents in 2016 (extended to non-residents 2020). No permit required for eligible adults.
laws.penalty: Carrying while prohibited: felony.
laws.exceptions: Firearms prohibited in schools, courts, and government buildings.

quiz.q: What type of carry law does Idaho have?
quiz.explanation: Idaho has constitutional — permitless carry for eligible adults — no permit required

laws.title: Background Check Requirements
laws.subtitle: Idaho Code §18 USC 922 — Federal NICS checks at licensed dealers
laws.fullDescription: All firearm purchases from licensed dealers in Idaho require a federal NICS background check. Idaho does not require background checks for private gun sales.
laws.penalty: Straw purchases or sales to prohibited persons: federal felony up to 10 years.
laws.exceptions: Transfers between immediate family members may be exempt.

quiz.q: Does Idaho require background checks for private gun sales?
quiz.explanation: Idaho only requires background checks for licensed dealer gun sales.

laws.title: Stand Your Ground / Castle Doctrine
laws.subtitle: Idaho Code §19-202A — Stand Your Ground
laws.fullDescription: Idaho has a Stand Your Ground law — no duty to retreat anywhere a person has a legal right to be.
laws.penalty: N/A — this law provides a defense against criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Force not justified if defender is committing a crime or the intruder is a co-resident.

quiz.q: Does Idaho have a Stand Your Ground law?

laws.title: Minimum Wage Law
laws.subtitle: Idaho Code §Labor Code — $7.25/hour minimum wage
laws.fullDescription: Idaho's minimum wage is $7.25/hour (2024). Idaho uses the federal minimum wage of $7.25/hr. No statewide increases have been passed.
laws.penalty: Employers violating minimum wage: back wages, double damages, and attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Tipped workers may have a lower base wage.

quiz.q: What is the minimum wage in Idaho?

laws.title: At-Will Employment
laws.subtitle: Idaho Code §Labor Code — Employment at will doctrine
laws.fullDescription: Idaho follows at-will employment. Employers may terminate for any legal reason; employees may quit anytime. at-will employment with standard exceptions.

laws.exceptions: Termination for illegal reasons (discrimination, retaliation) is prohibited.

quiz.q: Can an Idaho employer fire an employee without giving a reason?
quiz.explanation: Idaho is an at-will employment state — employers may generally terminate without cause.

laws.title: Right-to-Work Law — Yes
laws.subtitle: Idaho Code §Labor Code — Idaho is a right-to-work state

quiz.q: Is Idaho a right-to-work state?
quiz.explanation: Idaho is a right-to-work state.

laws.title: Non-Compete Agreement Enforceability

laws.fullDescription: Idaho: Non-compete agreements enforced if reasonable in scope and duration.

laws.fullDescription: Idaho unemployment insurance provides benefits to eligible workers. Maximum weekly benefit: $448 for up to 16 weeks. Workers must have earned at least $1500 in the base period.

laws.fullDescription: Idaho prohibits smoking in enclosed workplaces, restaurants, and bars.

laws.fullDescription: Idaho: Idaho requires helmets only for motorcycle riders under 18. Adults may ride without helmets.
